title: Length-aware selectivity for substring contains() scan filters
hypothesis: In q09 the scan filter on part is `contains(p_name,'<word>')` (LIKE '%x%' rewritten), stored as an ExpressionFilter. RelationStatisticsHelper::InspectTableFilter (relation_statistics_helper.cpp:446) ignores EXPRESSION_FILTER, so ExtractGetStats falls back to DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY=0.2: part est 400K (actual 109K, 5.4%), so lineitem⋈part is estimated at 12M when it is 3.27M. Because of this the probe pipeline ends up probing two large build sides: orders (15M rows, HASH_JOIN 2.9s CPU) and partsupp⋈supplier⋈nation (8M rows, HASH_JOIN 2.65s CPU). These are the two biggest operators after the lineitem scan (5.0s). Building a 15M/8M-row HT is mostly random memory writes. I forced the flipped plans (disabled_optimizers='join_order,build_side_probe_side' with an explicit join tree) so that lineitem⋈part (3.27M) is the build side and orders/partsupp are probed. Measured operator CPU: orders HJ 2.9s -> 2.0-2.2s, ps HJ 2.65s -> 1.67s. That is before any BF reaches those probe scans; see the other two issues. BuildProbeSideOptimizer::GetBuildSize/TryFlipJoinChildren needs the left estimate below about 10M rows to flip the orders join (narrow 2-col right side, 1.15 right-deep penalty), and below about 4.8M rows to flip the 8M partsupp join (the left side is wider). So the part selectivity estimate has to drop to about 0.06-0.08.
plan: In src/optimizer/join_order/relation_statistics_helper.cpp InspectTableFilter, add `case TableFilterType::EXPRESSION_FILTER`: cast to ExpressionFilter. If `expr` is a BoundFunctionExpression whose function name is `contains` (also accept `like`/`~~` patterns that are '%lit%' with no other wildcards, if they survive to here), with child[0] a column ref (or BoundReferenceExpression) and child[1] a non-NULL VARCHAR BoundConstantExpression with literal length L>=1, return cardinality * clamp(0.2 * 0.75^L, 0.01, 0.2), rounded up, minimum 1. Do NOT match NOT(...) or OR expressions; anything else keeps returning the input cardinality, so the existing default-0.2 path is unchanged. Because ExtractGetStats treats any reduction as 'has_equality_filter', the 0.2 fallback is then skipped for this table. Also check the CONJUNCTION_AND path, since contains may be ANDed with other filters on the same column. Check EXPLAIN on all 4 q09 instances (dark/deep/ghost/aquamarine, L=4..10): lineitem⋈part should become the build side of both the orders join and the partsupp join. Report which flips happened. Then run bench.
expected_gain: q09: -8..-15% (orders and ps joins together save about 1.5-2s CPU of about 14s in forced-plan tests). It is also the enabler for the BF-on-flipped-probe issues, which could bring q09 to about -30%.
generality: Any query with a positive substring predicate (LIKE '%x%', contains) on a dimension table that is joined to a fact table. Today such filters are all estimated at a flat 20%, which hides how selective they are. Longer literals are more selective, the same principle PostgreSQL's like selectivity uses. Plans can change for hidden templates that have positive contains filters. NOT LIKE (q13/q16 style) is excluded and unchanged.
risk: Medium-low. It is estimation only, so correctness is unaffected. A plan regression is possible if the true selectivity of a long literal is much higher than estimated (for example a common word). The 0.01 floor limits how far the estimate can drop.

title: Push join filters through compressed-materialization compress projections
hypothesis: Join filter pushdown runs after compressed materialization (optimizer.cpp: STATISTICS_PROPAGATION at line 289 inserts __internal_compress_integral_* projections; JOIN_FILTER_PUSHDOWN is at line 320). PushdownJoinFilterExpression (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:23) only passes column refs and integral casts, so a probe chain scan -> PROJECTION(__internal_compress_integral_uinteger(key, min)) -> join gets no dynamic filters at all. I observed this in the forced flipped q09 plan: the orders scan (15M rows) and the partsupp scan (8M) had no min/max and no BF, while the lineitem side did. Once the probe/build flip happens (contains-selectivity issue), BF on o_orderkey from 3.27M build keys would cut the orders probe from 15M rows to about 3.3M.
plan: In PushdownJoinFilterExpression, handle BOUND_FUNCTION whose function is one of the CM integral compress functions (__internal_compress_integral_*; see src/function/scalar/compressed_materialization/ and compressed_materialization_utils.hpp). Child 0 is the column, child 1 is the constant min offset. Record the offset in JoinFilterPushdownColumn (new field). In JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp:814), add the offset back to min/max before casting to the storage type. For BF: hashes are taken on the join-key values (compressed), so the BF cannot be used unless the build key is uncompressed in the same way. Simplest correct rule: allow the BF only when probe and build condition types match after decompression; otherwise push min/max only. Check how the build side key is compressed for this join first.
expected_gain: q09: 0% on the current plan. After the flip it could be -10% or more (orders join 2s CPU -> ~0.5s).
generality: Any hash join whose probe side scan key is compressed by CM before the join, which is common for integer FK keys with known ranges.
risk: Medium: offset arithmetic and type casts in filter values. A wrong offset gives wrong results, so it needs tests with non-zero min.

title: Bloom filter on one key of multi-condition equality hash joins
hypothesis: CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:775) requires ht->conditions.size()==1, so joins on (partkey, suppkey) never get a BF. After the flip, the partsupp probe (8M rows) joins on 2 keys against 3.27M build rows that hold only about 436K distinct partkeys. A BF on ps_partkey alone would drop about 95% of probe rows (forced plan: ps HJ 1.67s CPU while probing all 8M rows).
plan: Allow building a BF on a single equality condition column of a multi-condition join: hash only that column's build values during HT build, in a separate hash vector, and push BFTableFilter for that probe column. Choose the condition column with the highest estimated selectivity, or simply the first COMPARE_EQUAL condition. Requires JoinHashTable to compute the per-column hash (join_hashtable.cpp:720 InsertHashes currently uses the combined hash).
expected_gain: q09: ~-8% after the flip (ps HJ 1.67s -> ~0.3s CPU)
generality: Any multi-key equi-join with a selective build side, for example composite-FK joins.
risk: Medium: extra hash per build row; the BF must be keyed on the single-column hash.

title: Bloom filter on first equality key of multi-condition hash joins
hypothesis: Current best q09 plan (JSON profile of q09.m0): lineitem scan (59.99M rows, 2.95s CPU) probes HASH_JOIN with Conditions [l_partkey = p_partkey, l_suppkey = ps_suppkey] whose build side is part⋈partsupp (435,892 rows, ~109K distinct partkeys after contains() filter). The join outputs 3.27M rows (5.4%) but costs 2.84s CPU because all 60M rows are hashed on 2 keys and probed. The lineitem scan only gets min/max dynamic filters (l_partkey>=12 AND <=1999993, l_suppkey 1..100000), which prune nothing. No BF is pushed because JoinFilterPushdownInfo::CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:775) requires ht->conditions.size()==1, and JoinHashTable::Finalize (join_hashtable.cpp:775-796) feeds the BF the combined multi-column hash. A BF on l_partkey alone would drop ~94% of lineitem rows inside the scan (SelectivityOptionalFilter), shrinking the 2.84s probe to ~0.3s and skipping decode of the other 5 projected columns for dropped rows.
plan: 1) join_hashtable.cpp JoinHashTable::Finalize: when bloom_filter.IsInitialized() and conditions.size() > 1, for each chunk gather key column 0 from the rows (data_collection->Gather(chunk_state.row_locations, *FlatVector::IncrementalSelectionVector(), count, 0 /*first key column*/, key_vec, *FlatVector::IncrementalSelectionVector(), nullptr) with key_vec typed as conditions[0].right->return_type), compute VectorOperations::Hash(key_vec, bf_hashes, count) and bloom_filter.InsertHashes(bf_hashes, count). In InsertHashes, skip the combined-hash BF insert when conditions.size() > 1 (pass a flag or move the BF insert into Finalize). For single-key joins behaviour is unchanged (combined hash == single-column hash). 2) physical_hash_join.cpp CanUseBloomFilter: replace `ht->conditions.size() == 1` with: the filter's condition is HT condition 0 (pass join_condition[filter_idx] from FinalizeFilters, require == 0) and cmp == COMPARE_EQUAL and ht->conditions[0].comparison == COMPARE_EQUAL. PushBloomFilter already uses conditions[0] for key name/type and NullValuesAreEqual(0). Verify ReorderConditions puts equalities first so condition 0 is an equality, and that the HT layout's column 0 is condition 0's key. 3) Keep the existing guards (build_side_has_filter, probe est > HT count, !has_cast, not perfect HT). Add a sqllogictest: 2-key join with filtered build side, check results incl. NULL keys in either column and a build where key0 matches but key1 doesn't.
expected_gain: q09: lineitem HJ 2.84s -> ~0.4s CPU, plus some scan savings; total query CPU ~8.7s -> ~6s, so roughly -20..-30% wall.
generality: Any multi-column equi-join (composite FK, e.g. partsupp-style keys, multi-column joins in star schemas) where the build side is filtered and much smaller than the probe. SelectivityOptionalFilter self-disables when the BF is unselective, so the downside is the extra column gather+hash at HT finalize (proportional to build rows, small) and BF probe on the first few vectors.
risk: Low-medium. Correctness depends on hashing exactly the same column/type the probe-side BFTableFilter hashes; a mismatch drops valid rows. Gather of key 0 for each build chunk must use the right row-location vector. NULL semantics follow existing single-key logic.

title: Offset-aware join filter pushdown through CM integral compress projections (min/max + BF)
hypothesis: In the current best q09 plan (profile after E0002), the most expensive operator is the o_orderkey = l_orderkey HASH_JOIN at 2.22s CPU. orders (15M rows) probes a 3.27M-row build side, but only about 20% of the orders rows can match. The orders TABLE_SCAN has no dynamic filters at all because there is a PROJECTION __internal_compress_integral_uinteger(#0, 1) between the scan and the join. PushdownJoinFilterExpression (src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:23) only passes BOUND_COLUMN_REF and integral BOUND_CAST, so GetPushdownFilterTargets bails out at that projection. Both join sides are compressed with the same offset (the build-side projection is also __internal_compress_integral_uinteger(#0/#4, 1)), so the HT keys and BF hashes are compressed uint32 values c = key - min. Hash<uint32>(c) = MurmurHash64(uint64(c)) and Hash<int64>(k) = MurmurHash64(uint64(k)) (common/types/hash.hpp:36-60), so a probe key k matches a BF entry exactly when hash(k - offset) is used. A BF on o_orderkey should cut the orders probe from 15M to about 3M rows. That removes about 12M random probes into a hash table larger than 64MB (~1.2s CPU), and the BF itself costs about 0.15s CPU.
plan:
1) join_filter_pushdown.hpp: add to JoinFilterPushdownColumn an `bool has_offset=false; hugeint_t offset=0;` (or Value).
2) join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp PushdownJoinFilterExpression: add case BOUND_FUNCTION. If the function name starts with "__internal_compress_integral_", it has exactly 2 children, children[1] is a non-NULL BoundConstantExpression, filter.has_offset is false (only one level allowed), and child[0]'s type is integral with size <= 8 bytes, then set filter.offset = constant cast to HUGEINT and has_offset = true, and recurse into children[0]. Otherwise return false.
3) physical_hash_join.cpp JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters (~line 832): if pushdown_column.has_offset, cast min_val and max_val to HUGEINT, add the offset, then DefaultTryCastAs(storage_type), and `continue` on failure. Skip PushInFilter when has_offset, or add the offset to each value. For the BF (line 898-901), when has_offset, treat has_cast as false if storage_type is an integral type of at most 64 bits (excluding UBIGINT/UHUGEINT) and the condition type is integral. Pass the offset into PushBloomFilter, which needs a new optional int64 offset param.
4) bloom_filter.hpp/.cpp BFTableFilter: add an `int64_t key_offset` plus a `bool has_key_offset`, kept through the constructor, Copy and Serialize (optional property). In HashInternal, when has_key_offset is set, cast the (sliced) keys to a BIGINT state vector, subtract the offset (BinaryExecutor or a simple loop, preserving validity), then call VectorOperations::Hash on that vector. FilterValue: subtract too. CheckStatistics MUST return NO_PRUNING_POSSIBLE when has_key_offset, or else apply the offset in TemplatedCheckStatistics; otherwise zone-map pruning would be wrong.
5) Check that the deferred BF path (physical_hash_join.cpp:588 PushBloomFilter at finalize) carries the offset.
Tests: join a large table against a filtered table on an integer key whose min is non-zero (e.g. keys starting at 1000), with CM active (default). Compare results to the same query with `k+0` keys. Include NULL keys and negative-min keys.
expected_gain: q09: -12..-25%. The orders HJ (2.22s CPU of about 4.4s hot CPU) loses about 80% of its probe rows, and fewer rows flow through the orders compress projection.
generality: This applies to any hash join where CM compresses integer keys on the probe side before the join. That is common for FK joins on integer keys with known statistics ranges, for example TPC-H/DS fact-dimension joins where the probe side is not the bottom of a pipeline under a compress projection. Min/max dynamic filters through compress projections also enable zone-map pruning. A query could get slightly slower when the BF is unselective, but the SelectivityOptionalFilter self-disables in that case.
risk: Medium. The offset arithmetic and casts must be exact. CheckStatistics on a BF with an offset must not prune. Mixing signed and unsigned values: restrict to storage types up to int64/uint32. A wrong offset gives wrong results, which needs tests with a non-zero min and negative values.

title: Exact key bitmap mode for join BF on dense integer build keys
hypothesis: The lineitem scan carries the l_partkey BF and is the largest operator in q09 (5.28s CPU in the profile, 60M rows in, 3.27M out). The BF is sized for 436K build rows: 12 bits/key, next power of two = 8Mbit = 1MB. Each probe does a Murmur hash plus a random load into 1MB, which mostly misses L2. The build key range from min/max is 12..1999993, about 2M bits = 250KB. An exact bitmap indexed by (key - min) needs no hashing, fits L2 and has no false positives. A sibling run measured -15% on q21 with this mechanism (128 bits/key cap).
plan: In BloomFilter (src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp) add an exact mode, SetKeyRange(min, range), used when the build key is integral, range <= 128 * ht count and range <= 2^31. Insert/lookup become bit set/test on (key - min). Out-of-range probes are rejected. The probe side reads the raw key values instead of hashes. In FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp ~line 901) the min/max is known, so decide the mode there before the deferred build. JoinHashTable::InsertHashes/Finalize (join_hashtable.cpp) fills the bitmap from layout column 0 instead of hashes. CheckStatistics must handle the mode.
expected_gain: q09: -5..-10%, if the BF probe is a real part of the hot lineitem scan cost (unverified; cold profile).
generality: Any join BF whose build keys are dense integers, which is typical for surrogate keys and FKs.
risk: Medium. Two code paths in the BF, and must keep hash mode for non-integral keys. The hot gain is uncertain because an earlier decode-side tweak on this scan gave 0% hot.

title: Exact-bitmap join filter through CM integral compress projections (offset-shifted, no hashed BF)
hypothesis: Hot JSON profile of q09.m0 (505ms wall, ~3.4s CPU): HASH_JOIN o_orderkey=l_orderkey costs 1.39s CPU, the biggest operator (lineitem scan 0.77, lineitem HJ 0.51, agg 0.20). Its build side is 3.27M rows, so the pointer table is ~8M entries / 64MB. The probe side is all 15M orders rows, because the orders scan gets NO dynamic filter: scan -> PROJECTION(__internal_compress_integral_uinteger(o_orderkey,1)) -> HJ, and PushdownJoinFilterExpression (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:23) only passes colrefs and integral casts. About 80% of those probes miss, and each miss is a random cache miss into the 64MB table. E0003 already pushed min/max plus a HASHED BF through the compress projection. The orders rows fell 15M->2.96M, but bench was +4.7% (local -8.2%), because hashing 15M keys and doing random lookups into a ~5MB hashed BF cost about what it saved. What is different now: E0004 added exact-bitmap mode. Here the build keys span about 60M values with 3.27M keys, about 18 bits/key, under the 128 cap and under 2^31. So the orders scan filter becomes: subtract a constant, then do one bit test. There is no hashing, and because the probe-side keys arrive clustered or sorted (PK order), the walk through the 7.5MB bitmap is nearly sequential. It is also exact, so the HJ receives exactly the 3.27M matching rows.
plan: 1) Optimizer: in PushdownJoinFilterExpression (src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:23), accept a BOUND_FUNCTION whose name starts with __internal_compress_integral_ (see src/function/scalar/compressed_materialization/). Conditions: child 1 is a non-NULL constant castable to BIGINT, and child 0 is integral, at most 64 bits, and not UBIGINT. Recurse into child 0, then record `Value offset` on JoinFilterPushdownColumn (src/include/duckdb/execution/operator/join/join_filter_pushdown.hpp), and copy it wherever columns are rewritten (UNION children). TopN and RowGroupPruner also call GetPushdownFilterTargets: they must bail out when a target has an offset. 2) In JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp:870), when an offset is present: cast min/max to HUGEINT, add the offset, then cast to storage_type (skip the column if a cast fails); skip the IN filter. Compute has_cast against the decompressed storage type, so it does not by itself block the BF. 3) BF only in exact mode when there is an offset. Call TrySetExactBloomFilterRange (:845) with the build-side compressed min/max, unchanged. Its build_type==probe_type check must be relaxed for the offset case, because probe storage is BIGINT and the build is UINTEGER. If the HT BloomFilter is not exact after that call, do NOT push a hashed BF for an offset column (min/max only). 4) BFTableFilter (src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp plus its header): add an int64 key_offset/has_key_offset and serialize it as optional fields. In exact-mode Filter/FilterValue/CheckStatistics, test bit ((v - key_offset) - min) on the probe vector's own physical type. The existing out-of-range rejection must happen after the shift. If has_key_offset is set and the filter is not exact, the probe must never run (assert). 5) PushBloomFilter (:788) passes the offset of the pushdown column. Test: compare joins on real tables against `+0` versions (no pushdown), for example a count/sum of orders⋈lineitem with a lineitem-side filter. Confirm with EXPLAIN ANALYZE that the orders scan shows `IN BF` and that its cardinality drops.
expected_gain: q09: orders HJ 1.39s CPU -> ~0.5-0.7s, orders scan +~0.05s, so about -12..-20% wall. If bench shows <5%, the orders HJ is build-dominated (3.27M random inserts), and the next step would target the build rather than the probe.
generality: Any hash join whose probe-side integer key is CM-compressed before the join (common: CM compresses integer keys with known stats on both sides) and whose build keys are dense enough for the exact bitmap. Typical case: PK/FK joins where the fact-derived side is the build and the dimension or PK table is the probe. A query could get slower if the bitmap filter passes almost everything; SelectivityOptionalFilter pauses it then. Hashed BF behaviour is unchanged.
risk: Medium. The offset arithmetic must match the CM projection exactly: probe value v maps to (v - offset) and must equal the build's compressed key. Using the wrong offset or the wrong sign gives wrong results, so test with keys whose min is non-zero. TopN and RowGroupPruner must reject offset targets. Use only the probe-side offset from the compress expression on that side.

title: Software prefetch in join hash table probe and build for out-of-cache pointer tables
hypothesis: In the hot JSON profile (r6), the o_orderkey=l_orderkey HASH_JOIN costs 1.02s CPU even with E0005's probe filter (2.94M probe rows; 1.56s with the current best's 15M probe rows). That is the largest operator, about 30% of q09 CPU. The build has 3.27M rows, so the pointer table has about 8M entries (64MB) and the row data is about 180MB, both far bigger than cache. Each probe row costs about 2 dependent cache misses: entries[hash&mask] in ProbeForPointersInternal (join_hashtable.cpp:188-234), then the row-pointer dereference in row_matcher_build.Match (GetRowPointersInternal :294). The payload gather then hits the same row. Each build row costs 1 random miss in InsertHashesLoop (:591-715) when it loads and CASes entries[ht_offset]. None of these loops prefetch: grep finds no __builtin_prefetch in src/. The salt-probe loop has a data-dependent while/branch per row, which limits how many misses out-of-order execution can overlap. A group-prefetch pre-pass over the vector (up to 2048 independent addresses) turns serialized misses into overlapped ones. In the hash-join literature this typically gives a 1.3-2x speedup on probe loops once tables exceed the LLC.
plan: 1) Add a small portable helper (e.g. in src/include/duckdb/common/helper.hpp or locally in join_hashtable.cpp): `inline void PrefetchRead(const void *p)` that uses __builtin_prefetch(p, 0, 3) under `#if defined(__GNUC__) || defined(__clang__)` and does nothing otherwise. Add a write variant (rw=1). 2) ProbeForPointersInternal (join_hashtable.cpp:188): before the main loop, if ht.capacity * sizeof(ht_entry_t) exceeds a threshold (e.g. >= 1MB, i.e. beyond L2; a constant, not data-dependent), loop over i<count and prefetch &entries[hashes_dense[i] & ht.bitmask]. 3) GetRowPointersInternal (:282-295): after ProbeForPointers and before row_matcher_build.Match, prefetch the row pointers for the keys_to_compare_sel rows (pointers_result_v[row_index]). If layout row width > 64, also prefetch ptr+64 so the payload gather finds both lines in cache. Use the same size gate, based on data_collection size or capacity. 4) InsertHashesLoop (:591): after ApplyBitmaskAndGetSaltBuild, with the same gate, prefetch-for-write &entries[ht_offsets[remaining_sel->get_index(i)]] for all rows before the while loop. 5) Optionally, in ScanStructure chain following (pointer next loads in the Next/AdvancePointers path), prefetch the next pointers before gathering. Do this only if it is trivial. No semantic change: prefetch is only a hint.
expected_gain: q09: orders HJ 1.0-1.5s CPU, maybe -25..-40%, giving about -6..-12% wall. lineitem⋈partsupp HJ (0.51s, 436K-row build, about 1M entries/8MB, exceeds L2) maybe -10..-20%. Total q09 roughly -5..-12%.
generality: Every hash join whose build side exceeds L2/LLC, which covers most large-fact-table joins (TPC-H q09/q18/q21-like, star joins with big dimensions). Small HTs are gated off, so there is no extra work there. Worst case is a few ns per row of wasted prefetch instructions on mid-size tables that already fit in LLC.
risk: Low: correctness cannot change, since prefetch is a hint. Performance risk is small: the pre-pass adds one loop over hashes per vector, about 1ns/row. Portability is covered by the compiler-guarded macro.

title: Re-land exact-bitmap join filter through CM compress (E0005) plus group prefetch in the HT probe and build
hypothesis: E0005 (exact bitmap BF plus shifted min/max through __internal_compress_integral_* projections) was a real gain: q09 local bench went 525->450 ms (-14.3%) and the full bench was -7.9%, with hidden validation ok. It was retired only because that bench run's noise band was wider than the gain. The orders scan drops from 15M to 2.94M rows. Its own profile shows what is left: the o_orderkey HASH_JOIN still costs about 1.0-1.35s CPU, which is the largest operator. The 3.27M-row build means a pointer table of about 8M entries (64MB) and about 180MB of row data, and neither ProbeForPointersInternal (join_hashtable.cpp:188) nor InsertHashesLoop (:591) prefetches. A grep finds no __builtin_prefetch anywhere in src/. Each probe row costs a dependent miss on entries[] plus the row-pointer dereference in RowMatcher, and each build row costs a random CAS miss. Re-landing E0005 together with a group prefetch pass targets the same join from both sides (fewer probe rows, cheaper misses per row), so the combined change should clear the noise gate.
plan: Part A, the E0005 re-implementation as described in the ledger: (1) In PushdownJoinFilterExpression (src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:23), accept BOUND_FUNCTION __internal_compress_integral_*(x, const) when x is a signed or unsigned integral type of 64 bits or less (not UBIGINT) and the const is non-NULL and castable to BIGINT. Record a `Value offset` on JoinFilterPushdownColumn (join_filter_pushdown.hpp), copy it in UNION child rewrites, and allow only one offset per column. TopN and RowGroupPruner must bail out when a target has an offset (they reuse GetPushdownFilterTargets). (2) FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp ~870): for offset columns, cast min/max to HUGEINT, add the offset, then cast to the storage type, and skip the column if the cast fails. Skip the IN filter. Push the BF only when TrySetExactBloomFilterRange (:845) made the filter exact; never push a hashed BF for an offset column. (3) BFTableFilter: add has_key_offset/key_offset, serialized as optional fields 203/204. Filter, FilterValue and CheckStatistics test bit (v - offset - key_min) in wrapping uint64 arithmetic, and the stats range check uses hugeint. A non-exact filter with an offset lets every row through. (4) PushBloomFilter (:788) passes the first key's offset and storage type. Part B, prefetch in src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp only: add a local inline helper that wraps __builtin_prefetch under #if __GNUC__||__clang__. Gate it on ht capacity*sizeof(ht_entry_t) >= 1MB. In ProbeForPointersInternal, run a pre-pass that prefetches &entries[hash & bitmask] for every row. In GetRowPointersInternal, prefetch the row pointers of keys_to_compare_sel before row_matcher_build.Match. In InsertHashesLoop, prefetch-for-write entries[ht_offsets[...]] before the while loop. Test correctness by comparing results against `+0` keys, including a dense build whose bitmap is active.
expected_gain: q09: -10..-18% (E0005 alone measured -7.9..-14.3%; prefetch maybe another -3..-8% on the 1s-CPU orders HJ and the 0.5s lineitem-partsupp HJ)
generality: Part A covers any hash join whose probe-side integer FK key is compressed by compressed materialization, which is common for joins above CM projections. Part B covers every hash join whose build side exceeds L2, which includes most fact-fact joins. Small hash tables are gated off. The worst case is about 1ns/row wasted on mid-size tables.
risk: Medium. Part A's offset arithmetic was validated in E0005 (hidden ok), but only with offset 1. Re-implementing it carries a transcription risk, so test with a dense build. Part B cannot change results because prefetch is only a hint.
